offence_severity: Minimum: 6 months to maximum: life imprisonment
physical_harm: Death of one person and injury to another
key_evidence_accepted: The eye-witnesses including the informant have offered a consistent, coherent and convincing narration thereof which does not admit of any doubt of their trustworthiness. The medical evidence reveals injuries on the deceased and the injured compatible with the weapon used.
witness_credibility: The plea of their family relationship to discredit them does not commend for acceptance in the attendant facts and circumstances.
trial_duration: Dates of offence: 06.07.2002; Trial judgment: 01.10.2008; High Court decision: 01.10.2008; Supreme Court decision: 02.12.2016
legal_representation: Counsel for the accused: Yatinder Singh, Sr. Adv., Arijeet Singh, Ms. Aprajita A Anvita; Counsel for the State: Saurabh Ajay Gupta, AAG., Ms. Naresh Bakshi, Saurabh Singhal, Nishant Bishnoi
investigation_status: FIR registered, charge-sheet filed, trial completed
appeal_history: Trial court: Conviction under Sections 302 and 307 IPC; High Court: Affirmed conviction and sentence; Supreme Court: Partly allowed appeal, conviction converted to Sections 304 Part 1 and 307 IPC, sentence reduced to period already undergone
prosecution_argument: The prosecution argued that the appellant had committed the offence under Sections 302 and 307 IPC, and that the evidence, including eye-witnesses and medical evidence, proved the case beyond doubt. They also contended that the co-accused's acquittal did not affect the appellant's guilt.
defence_argument: The defence argued that the prosecution failed to prove the charge against the appellant, citing the acquittal of the co-accused and the family relationship of the witnesses as undermining their credibility. They also claimed that no case for murder or attempt was proved.
legal_principle_applied: The court applied the principle that the prosecution must prove the case beyond reasonable doubt, and that the acquittal of a co-accused does not affect the conviction of another accused.
sentencing_rationale: The sentence was reduced to the period already undergone due to the time elapsed since the incident, the appellant's uncontrollable fit of anger, and the lack of intent to eliminate any of those fired at.
judicial_mitigating_factors: The court considered the time elapsed since the incident, the root cause of the incident, and the appellant's uncontrollable fit of anger which deprived him of self-control.
other_sentence_order: The appellant was ordered to be set at liberty forthwith, if not required to be detained in connection with any other case.
